Direct proof: first show the primitive triple is pairwise coprime and exactly one leg is even; interchange so x odd and y even, hence z odd. Set A=(z+x)/2 and B=(z-x)/2. Then A,B are positive coprime integers and AB=(y/2)^2. Unique prime factorization forces A=m^2 and B=n^2. Recover x=m^2-n^2, y=2mn, z=m^2+n^2; A>B gives m>n, coprimality descends to m,n, and x odd forces opposite parity. Converse follows by the identity and a prime-divisor argument for gcd(x,y,z).
